title: Transformations and Function Operations
description: A parent function is a convenient reference member identified by domain, range, symmetry, endpoints, asymptotes, and rate patterns.
outcomes: Recognize benchmark function families by domain, range, symmetry, intercepts, end behavior, and rate patterns.
Derive graph transformations by tracking how input-output pairs move.
Analyze how adding a constant outside a function changes outputs, range, intercepts, extrema, and asymptotes.
Analyze how replacing x by x-h changes input locations, domain, intercepts, extrema, and vertical asymptotes.
Reflect function graphs across coordinate axes and connect reflection rules with even and odd symmetry.
Distinguish output scaling from input scaling and determine the resulting stretches, compressions, domains, and ranges.
Analyze and graph functions with several transformations by tracking inputs, outputs, and key features.
Add and subtract functions pointwise, determine the common domain, and interpret combined outputs.
Multiply and divide functions pointwise while analyzing zeros, restrictions, and combined graph behavior.
Use parent-family features, transformations, and one or more data points to construct and verify a function formula.
